steps.title: Prepare the Station
steps.subtitle: Set up, inspect, clean, and document the Samsung DDR5 test station.

items.text: Place the tester on a flat ESD-protected surface. Connect monitor, keyboard, VGA, and approved power.
Verify ventilation and keep the tester top panel installed during operation.
Inspect the tester, connectors, and slots. Clean slots with approved dry air.
Record date, technician, part number, serial numbers, quantity, and planned aging duration.

steps.warning: Stop for socket damage, broken DIMM hardware, contamination, smoke, odor, or repeated electrical/boot abnormalities.

steps.title: Load Samsung DDR5 Modules
steps.subtitle: Load only Samsung DDR5 modules with power disconnected.

items.text: Unplug tester power and wait at least 30 seconds before loading.
Handle each module by its edges. Align it to the assigned slot and press evenly with both hands until fully seated.
Load 1 to 8 modules, maximum one module per channel.
Record and verify each serial number against its channel and slot.

steps.warning: Do not rock, twist, or force a module. Never insert or remove memory while power is connected.

steps.title: Verify BIOS Settings
steps.subtitle: Complete on initial setup or after BIOS settings have been reset.

items.text: Apply power and press Del during boot to enter BIOS.
Set the current date and time.
In Memory Test, select Samsung Test and enable TestPattern 1 through 9.
In Boot, confirm CentOS is Boot Option 1.
Press F4 to save and exit.

steps.warning: Start BIOS-level testing with no USB drive connected.

steps.title: Run BIOS-Level Test 1
steps.subtitle: Run all nine Samsung STEP BIOS patterns.

items.text: Confirm no USB drive is connected, then apply power. The BIOS test starts automatically.
Review the on-screen result by channel when the test completes.
Mark every failed module immediately and record the failed item.
Unplug power and wait at least 30 seconds.
Remove only modules that failed Test 1 by releasing the socket sides and lifting by the edges.

steps.warning: A failure in any required BIOS or OS test is a module failure under the one-strike rule.

steps.title: Run BIOS-Level Test 2
steps.subtitle: Retest all modules that passed the first BIOS test.

items.text: Leave previously passed modules installed and confirm no USB drive is connected.
Reapply power and allow the second automatic BIOS test to finish.
Record and mark any newly failed module.
Unplug power, wait 30 seconds, and remove newly failed modules.
Verify BIOS logs in /root/LOG_BIOS. Expected filename pattern: SAMSUNG_OSV_time.log.

steps.warning: Confirm the log includes channel, pass/fail, failed item, and serial number.

steps.title: Run OS-Level Aging
steps.subtitle: Use the duration approved for the number of modules loaded.

items.text: At the operating-system prompt run an approved aging command.
Recommended duration: 1-2 modules = 5 minutes; 3-4 = 10 minutes; 5-6 = 20 minutes; 7-8 = 30 minutes.
Use only a command available on the tester and approved for the module density and lot.
Review the final result and identify failed channels or slots.
Mark and segregate every failed module.
Verify aging logs in /root/LOG_AGING. Expected filename pattern: SAMSUNG_DEC_time.log.

steps.warning: Only modules passing both BIOS runs and OS aging may return to production.

steps.title: Copy Logs and Finish
steps.subtitle: Copy all required evidence after testing is complete.

items.text: Insert a FAT32-formatted USB drive only after testing is complete.
Run ./usb at the prompt.
Verify both BIOS and aging logs are present on the USB.
Unplug power, wait 30 seconds, then remove all modules and the USB.
Archive logs on the controlled workstation by test date, update the OSV report, and submit through the approved internal method.

steps.warning: Do not remove modules before disconnecting power and completing the 30-second wait.

steps.title: Recover from Hang or No Video
steps.subtitle: Isolate abnormal BIOS or OS aging behavior.

items.text: For red error text, frozen display, black screen over 10 minutes, or LED off: unplug power and wait 30 seconds.
If multiple modules were loaded, test one module at a time to isolate the failure.
Treat missing module information in the BIOS log as a possible no-video failure.
For an OS aging hang, reboot safely and run ./hang at the OS prompt.
Use the generated /root/LOG_AGING hang log to identify the failing module. If no information appears, repeat the test once.

steps.warning: Stop if physical socket or module damage is found.

steps.title: Classify and Disposition
steps.subtitle: Apply the one-strike acceptance rule.

items.text: Pass BIOS Test 1, BIOS Test 2, and OS aging: return to production subject to site release requirements.
Any BIOS or OS failure: segregate for Samsung RMA or failure analysis.
Physical damage: stop testing and route through the site damage process.
Unresolved hang or no-video: keep segregated and escalate with logs, identity, channel, and test history.
Complete the technician checklist and test record before closeout.

steps.warning: Do not apply this procedure to SK hynix, Micron, DDR4, or another vendor platform.
